text:
ConocoPhillips rose barely 0.08% today as oil prices fell on easing geopolitical tension. Yesterday (October 28th), prospects of U.S. strikes on Iran had pushed oil prices higher, but today renewed U.S.-Iran peace negotiations reversed that fear premium—crude dropped from its recent highs, which weighed on the stock despite a two-week rally that had lifted it 5.25% from late October lows.

The broader picture is one of volatile Middle East risk. Over the past two days, the market swung sharply as headlines shifted from military escalation risk (pushing oil and the stock up) to diplomatic hopes (pushing both down today). With U.S. crude at $103/barrel and global crude at $123/barrel, the company remains exposed to this geopolitical yo-yo, and today's flat performance reflects how quickly sentiment can flip on peace talk developments.
